ops.title: daemonkit export surface measured: 1,272 exported — 495 public, 617 internal-only, 125 dead
ops.body:
Measured 2026-07-27 at `origin/main` = `1d55b2a` (v0.20.10 an ancestor) by the Phase-0 export-census lane, using a `go/packages` type-checked reference extraction across daemonkit plus all 10 fleet consumers. Raw data: `/tmp/dk-phase0/inventory.json` (740 KB), per-repo refs in `/tmp/dk-phase0/refs-<repo>.json`, allowlist checked in at `ci/exported.txt`, extractor at `ci/exportcensus/main.go`.

**This corrects the remediation plan's estimates, which were wrong in both directions.**

| | plan estimate | measured |
|---|---|---|
| exported symbols | 747 | **1,272** |
| zero fleet callers | 366 (49%) | **125 (9.8%)** |
| external callers exist | ~381 | **495** |
| daemonkit-internal only | — | **617** |
| unresolved | — | **35** |

Reference counts per consumer (type-checked, 0 package errors everywhere): daemonkit 11,829 · captain-hook 601 · cc-interact 558 · synckit 535 · cc-notes 513 · cc-orchestrate 201 · cc-present 106 · binrun 81 · cc-review 56 · cc-patch 32 · reposync 31.

**What this changes.**

1. **The surface is 70% larger than believed** — 1,272, not 747. The earlier figure undercounted methods on exported types and struct fields of exported types.
2. **Far less is outright dead.** Only 125 symbols (9.8%) have no caller anywhere. The "delete ~366 dead symbols" framing does not survive contact with the data; the real shape of the collapse is **unexport 617, delete 125**, which is a much safer operation — unexporting is invisible to a consumer that never called it, and the fleet-build gate proves that per-symbol before any tag.
3. **495 symbols have real external callers.** Reaching the ~150-exported target therefore requires *removing capability or reshaping it into assemblies*, not just deleting orphans. Every one of those 495 must land on the Phase-0 parity checklist as kept, replaced-by-an-assembly, or dropped-with-reason. This is the single biggest scope correction to the plan.
4. **35 unresolved** — symbols reached only through an interface, an embedded struct, or a struct-literal field, which a selector-based census cannot settle. These need an LSP or manual pass before any deletion wave touches them. Treat unresolved as PUBLIC-API until proven otherwise.

The `ci/exported.txt` allowlist plus `scripts/export-census.sh` now fail CI on **any** difference in either direction — additions and removals both — so a deletion wave has to land exactly what the census approved.
